edges.effect_quant: A 2018 meta-analysis of 50 studies including 8,398 IBS patients and 1,432 controls found a pooled SIBO prevalence of 38% in IBS and an odds ratio of 4.7 (95% CI 3.1-7.2) versus controls; methane-positive overgrowth was not elevated across all IBS cases in a 2021 meta-analysis, but was more common in constipation-predominant IBS than diarrhea-predominant IBS (OR 3.1, 95% CI 1.7-5.6).
edges.population: adults with irritable bowel syndrome evaluated for bacterial overgrowth using breath testing or small-bowel aspirate culture, including subtype analyses
edges.mechanism: Small-intestinal bacterial overgrowth can increase gas production, bile acid deconjugation, low-grade inflammation, and altered fermentation patterns that plausibly worsen bloating, pain, stool urgency, or constipation depending on the dominant microbial profile.
edges.summary: The overlap between SIBO and IBS symptoms is one of the stronger microbiome-gut disorder associations in the literature, especially when breath-test-defined overgrowth is compared against healthy controls. What remains less certain is how much of the signal reflects a direct causal driver of IBS symptoms versus a marker of subgroup biology, particularly in constipation-predominant disease.
edges.caveats: Diagnostic methods vary widely, breath tests are imperfect, and prevalence estimates change materially by substrate and cutoff. Treatment-response data support the general bacterial-overgrowth hypothesis, but they do not prove that every positive breath test is the main cause of a given patient's symptoms.
